To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a glutathione peroxi- dase has been purified from the Aloe plant, which has a low molecular weight and contains selenium.

the Aloe vera GSHPx is a tetrameric enzyme, with one atom of Se per subunit; the enzyme is competitively, and specifically, inhibited by the glyoxalase inhibitor N, S, Bis-FMOC-glutathione; the enzyme has a molecular weight of 64 kD, with four subunits of 16 kD; the enzyme is a selenium containing enzyme, with a specific activity of 0.3 units/mg of protein.
Aloe vera extracts contain a GSHPx that is similar to the GSHPx from animal sources in that it is a selenium-dependent enzyme that is inhibited by N, Fmoc-glutathione.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification and characterization of a novel glutathione peroxi-dase from the A. vera plant.
the purification and characterization of a glutathione peroxide from the aloe vera plant.
the identification, isolation, purification, and characterization of a glutathione peroxide from the Aloe plant.

the GSHPx from A. vera has the same characteristics as the glutathione peroxides from animal sources, but that the enzyme is not identical with the GSHPx isolated from human erythrocytes.

the Aloe vera glutathione peroxidease is a glyoxalase, and that it is not a glutathione peroxidaselike enzyme.
